issues.title: [Performance][v0.30.0] Match DSA O-proj exchanges to runtime batches
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The releases/v0.30.0 counterpart of #19237.

DSA O-projection TP currently uses its allocated buffer capacity for every collective and projection, even when the current decode graph bucket is much smaller. For example, a 480-token profiling allocation makes a later 96-token bucket exchange and project 480 rows per source rank.

Separate the allocation capacity from the execution length. Keep the existing capacity-sized buffers, but repack each exchange into a contiguous prefix sized to the current batch. All-to-all, wo_a, wo_b and reduce-scatter use that execution length. Prefix views retain their original device addresses; slicing the middle dimension of [OTP, capacity, ...] would leave gaps between peers. Profiling executes its full batch once. Zero-row direct calls retain a one-row exchange.

**Tradeoff: this adds a DP metadata synchronization compared with the current skip-DP path.** When O-proj TP size is greater than one, retain the runner's existing CPU DP all-reduce so ranks select a common graph bucket. This is once per forward rather than once per attention layer; O-proj's per-layer collective count is unchanged. Restoring coordination also restores uniform runner padding across DP ranks. The CPU synchronization and extra padding can offset projection savings; end-to-end performance has not been established.

Refs #17961. #19190 separately changes buffer ownership/sharing and profiling behavior. This patch retains per-layer ownership and full profiling shapes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Runtime O-proj exchanges and projections follow the current coordinated bucket instead of the maximum allocation capacity. Resident buffer capacity remains max(decode capacity, scheduler token budget); this change does not reduce that allocation. No new option is added.

### How was this patch tested?

- **30 focused isolated CPU cases passed on each branch**, executing exact production methods and repository test functions with kernel/collective/import substitutes. Coverage includes full profiling in one call, smaller/larger/smaller runtime batches, contiguous peer layout, unchanged buffer addresses, FP8/BF16, OTP2/8, empty inputs, oversize rejection, non-OTP/PCP behavior, and retaining DP coordination for OTP sizes greater than one. On the main unmodified base, 22 of these cases fail and 8 pass.
- **Real Ascend 950, OTP2, torch_npu/HCCL/ACL graphs: 44 numerical comparisons per rank passed on each branch, maximum absolute baseline/candidate difference 0.** BF16/FP8, one/two groups per rank, changing inputs, full/small/zero rows, and non-monotonic bucket replay were exercised. Device pointers remained stable.
- Unequal and idle rank tests also executed the verified upstream DP dispatch/synchronization functions with a small graph-bucket selector and real Gloo CPU synchronization, followed by real HCCL graph replay. Agreed buckets were [1, 6, 12, 0, 1], including all-idle dispatch without a forward. This is an isolated integration harness, not complete runner/model serving coverage.
- Environment: image a40785261e55, CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, A5 host .22 physical devices 4/5. These devices reported power-telemetry warnings; numerical checks completed, but no performance measurement is claimed.
- Pinned Ruff 0.14 check/format, codespell, compilation, targeted import/context/long-function checks and git diff --check passed. Focused mypy for Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 passed for dsa_v1.py and both test files. Local utils.py checking reports two pre-existing var-annotated errors in unrelated compressed-metadata code; the same errors were reproduced on the main baseline.
- Full native repository UT collection is not established in the available environment because its installed vLLM API differs from these branches. Full format.sh ci was attempted but external actionlint environment setup did not complete. Current-head full CI, full-model accuracy, torch.compile/serving integration, and end-to-end performance including restored CPU DP coordination remain pending. **Keep this PR draft.**

Focused repository commands in a matching environment:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py -k 'o_proj_exchange_uses_current_batch or non_otp_dummy_projection_keeps_full_batch or a5_fp8_o_proj_keeps_otp_collectives'
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/test_utils.py -k oproj_tp_requires_dp_shape_coordination
```

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

issues.title: [BugFix][SpecDecode] Enable replicated DFlash drafts with PCP on MRV2
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Starting Model Runner V2 with PCP and a DFlash draft currently fails with `Ascend MRV2 PCP supports speculative decoding only with MTP, Eagle3 and DSpark.` This change enables the replicated DFlash/DFlash2 draft path and addresses the distributed behavior needed after that validation succeeds:

- Negotiate draft batch capacity from the restored global requests instead of reusing the PCP-local target DP counts.
- Synchronize completed draft tokens and probability distributions on paired vLLM versions that do not provide `PCPManager.sync_drafts`; use the upstream runner hook when available.
- Merge DFlash2 candidate TopK values and token IDs across PCP as well as TP when the shared target LM head has PCP-sharded vocabulary weights.

The implementation uses the existing Ascend speculator and model overrides. It introduces no new monkey patch or environment variable. The fallback proposal synchronization can be removed once all supported paired vLLM versions provide the runner hook.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `--prefill-context-parallel-size > 1` can be combined with `method="dflash"` on Model Runner V2. The context-parallel documentation and release note `release_notes/fragments/21630.yaml` accompany the change. Existing encoder-decoder, LoRA and FULL-graph restrictions remain in place.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests:** 199 passed in the Ascend container:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash_pcp.py \
  tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash2_v2.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_manager_v2.py \
  --disable-warnings --maxfail=3
```

Coverage includes PCP-enabled/disabled draft capacity, profiling and dummy calls, old/new upstream synchronization hooks, probabilistic request-slot writeback, padded vocabulary entries, PCP-only/TP-only/PCP+TP candidate selection, and the existing unsupported-configuration checks.

**Hardware smoke test:** two nodes with eight Ascend 950DT NPUs each; vLLM 0.33.0 (`4ba787e`), vLLM Ascend `06a25402991cae7fb198f99d66c22b390647a219` plus this fix. Model: GLM-5.3 W8A8C8/MXFP8 with a GLM-5.3-DFlash2 draft. Configuration: PCP=8, TP=1, PP=2, EP enabled, eager execution, one speculative token, async scheduling, prefix caching, FP8 target KV cache, draft KV dtype `auto`, max model length 135000, max batched tokens 16384, max sequences 500, GPU memory utilization 0.95, PP layer partition 42/36.

- Health and model-list endpoints returned HTTP 200.
- A short arithmetic request returned `2` with `finish_reason="stop"`.
- Four concurrent requests returned the expected `10`, `11`, `12`, `13`, all with normal completion.
- A 19,224-token input exercised chunked prefill and returned the requested `READY` with normal completion.
- Draft acceptance counters advanced; both node logs had no runtime errors during these checks.

This is functional smoke coverage, not a throughput or numerical-accuracy benchmark. The full 135000-token limit, graph-mode execution and broader model coverage still need CI/reviewer validation. The draft PR is rebased onto current upstream `main`; the hardware results above identify the exact container baseline used.

**Static checks:** Ruff 0.14.0 lint and formatting, codespell, the boolean-context-manager check, and `git diff --check` passed for the affected files. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted twice but stopped while nodeenv downloaded the Markdown lint environment (`http.client.IncompleteRead`); the complete repository hook run remains pending. A separate Markdown lint installation was also blocked by an npm certificate-chain error; Markdown lint remains pending in CI.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage
- [x] Regression test
- [x] Error / failure path coverage
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests
- [ ] Performance impact: functional NPU validation is recorded above; no performance claim is made.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58
